_meta.purpose: User-facing experiment / mission-objective scenarios. Each one maps onto an EXISTING mission profile in data/purposes.json; scoring, gates and target compatibility are still computed by model/recommend.py. This file only adds labels, explanations and NASA source links.

classification.direct: NASA publishes an activity/objective that directly matches this scenario.
classification.related: NASA publishes a closely related analog activity or objective; ASTRANOVUS maps it onto this scenario.
classification.indirect: NASA documents only general analog/testing context; the scenario itself is an ASTRANOVUS proposal.

_meta.notice: These are candidate user-facing categories proposed by ASTRANOVUS. They are NOT claims that NASA has scheduled or endorsed each described experiment.

experiments.name: Water-ice prospecting & resource-utilization field testing
experiments.what_is_tested: Drilling, sampling and processing of ice-bearing frozen ground with sensors and hardware that must work in extreme cold.
experiments.why: Water ice is a candidate resource for life support and propellant, so teams need cold, dry, ice-bearing ground to rehearse prospecting and extraction before flight.

nasa_documented.summary: NASA lists In-Situ Resource Utilization among its analog capabilities and describes field analog sites used to test equipment for the Moon and Mars.

cannot_reproduce: Lunar permanently shadowed regions are far colder than any Earth surface
Vacuum and 1/6 g (Moon surface gravity)
Lunar ice origin, age and chemistry

experiments.name: Lunar rover mobility & navigation testing
experiments.what_is_tested: Slope climbing, obstacle crossing, autonomous navigation and landing-style hazard avoidance on bare, rough, rocky ground.
experiments.why: Rovers must cross rugged, sparsely vegetated terrain with long shadows; unvegetated rough terrain on Earth lets engineers test traction and autonomy.

nasa_documented.summary: NASA/JPL field-tested the ERNEST prototype rover in the Colorado Desert (March 2026), running at dusk, dawn and night to mimic the long shadows of the Moon's polar regions, with obstacle tests in JPL's Mars Yard.

cannot_reproduce: 1/6 g changes wheel-soil loads and slip
Lunar regolith is sharper and more electrostatic than Earth sand
No atmosphere (dust and thermal behaviour differ)

experiments.name: Regolith & dust-related equipment evaluation

extra_gates.why: rain/humidity would invalidate dust tests (same threshold used by the POWER_THERMAL mission profile)

experiments.draft_assumption: ASTRANOVUS-proposed variation of the MOBILITY profile: extra weight and gate on dryness. Draft - not NASA-verified.
experiments.what_is_tested: How seals, joints, wheels and optics behave in dry, fine, abrasive ground material.
experiments.why: Dust and regolith wear is a documented Artemis hardware risk. Because NASA stresses that simulant composition changes the result, natural dry, barren Earth ground complements (does not replace) laboratory simulant testing.
applications: Dust-contamination tests on optics and connectors

nasa_documented.summary: NASA's lunar dust mitigation roadmap lists Taber abrasion, dust adhesion and surface-energy tests with regolith-simulant abrasive wheels as standard Artemis hardware tests, warns that results vary strongly with the simulant (lunar soil composition differs by location) and recommends more than one simulant. These are laboratory tests; NASA's sources checked do not describe testing at natural Earth sites, which is the ASTRANOVUS proposal.

cannot_reproduce: Lunar dust is electrostatically charged and extremely abrasive
Vacuum changes dust transport
Earth air and humidity alter adhesion

experiments.name: Power, illumination & thermal environment testing
experiments.what_is_tested: Solar power, batteries and hardware under strong day-night temperature swings and extreme or low-angle lighting.
experiments.why: Surface systems must survive extreme thermal cycling and long darkness; dry, high-swing Earth sites let teams rehearse thermal-cycling and insulation tests, but cannot reproduce multi-week lunar night or vacuum.
applications: Solar-array performance in low sun angle

nasa_documented.summary: NASA Fission Surface Power material documents the problem this scenario addresses: polar night temperatures of about 50-100 K, nights lasting up to ~14.5 Earth days, and battery mass limits. It describes systems and requirements, not an Earth analog field campaign; the rover test at dusk/dawn/night simulates lunar polar lighting for mobility only.

cannot_reproduce: Lunar day/night cycle lasts about two Earth weeks
Vacuum: no convective cooling
Lunar polar permanent shadow / near-permanent sunlight geometry

experiments.name: Habitat & surface operations rehearsal
experiments.what_is_tested: Habitat construction, regolith handling, shelter concepts and crew workflows in an isolated, harsh site.
experiments.why: Long stays need shelters and procedures validated in remote analog environments before use.

nasa_documented.summary: NASA's Artemis Base Camp plan includes a foundation surface habitat for up to four crew and frames the base camp as a testbed for Mars-surface analog operations; NASA's analog pages describe habitat/isolation analogs (HERA, Antarctic stations) and lava-tube mapping at Lava Beds National Monument.

cannot_reproduce: Radiation exposure is far higher on the Moon
1/6 g and vacuum
Micrometeoroid environment

experiments.name: Geological sampling & astronaut fieldwork
experiments.what_is_tested: Sampling procedures, field geology workflows and crew training on rocky, dry, little-vegetated terrain.
experiments.why: Astronauts and scientists practise recognising, documenting and collecting rocks in analog terrain.

nasa_documented.summary: NASA's analogs page describes desert rover/geology testing and Artemis crew training at analog sites and pairs Meteor Crater with the Moon's Copernicus crater; a NASA advisory-committee record cites ground analogs such as DesertRATS-Lite in Arizona.

cannot_reproduce: Lunar rock types and ages differ from most Earth rock
No weathering or biology on the Moon
Suited operations in vacuum and 1/6 g

experiments.name: Rover mobility & autonomous navigation testing
experiments.what_is_tested: Driving, slope and obstacle crossing, and autonomous path planning on barren, rocky or sandy terrain.
experiments.why: Rovers must cross unvegetated, rocky and sandy terrain; Earth analog terrain lets teams validate mobility and autonomy.

nasa_documented.summary: NASA/JPL's ERNEST rover campaign (Colorado Desert, March 2026) tested mobility and reinforcement-learning autonomy for future Moon rovers and says it could apply to Mars; obstacle tests were run in JPL's Mars Yard.

cannot_reproduce: Mars gravity is about 0.38 g
Thin CO2 atmosphere (about 6 mbar)
Martian soil mechanics and dust differ from Earth sand

experiments.name: Geological sampling & sedimentary exploration
experiments.what_is_tested: Rock and soil sampling, stratigraphy reading and sample-caching procedures in dry, rock-exposed terrain.
experiments.why: Mars science aims to read the planet's crustal and surface history; analog geology lets teams practise sampling and context documentation.

nasa_documented.summary: Perseverance's stated objectives include studying Jezero Crater's geology and caching the most promising rock and soil samples; NASA's Mars science objectives include a geology goal.

cannot_reproduce: Martian rocks formed under different conditions and ages
No Earth-like biology or weathering history
Atmosphere and gravity differ

experiments.name: Astrobiology & biosignature-detection instrument testing
experiments.what_is_tested: Instruments and protocols that look for signs of past life in ancient, dry sedimentary or mineral settings.
experiments.why: Searching for biosignatures needs instruments proven on real Earth rocks and soils that preserve (or lack) traces of life.

nasa_documented.summary: Perseverance's objectives include determining whether Jezero's ancient environments were habitable and searching for signs of past microbial life; NASA's Mars science objectives include a Life and Habitability goal; NASA's analogs page cites soil sampling in Chile's Atacama Desert.

experiments.shares_profile_note: Uses the same SCIENCE mission profile as geology & sampling; the reference site you choose differentiates the ranking.
cannot_reproduce: Earth life contaminates Earth samples in ways not present on Mars
Martian radiation and perchlorate chemistry
Different atmosphere and gravity

experiments.name: Subsurface ice exploration & resource-utilization research
experiments.what_is_tested: Detecting, drilling and processing ice-rich ground in cold, dry, mid-to-high latitude terrain.
experiments.why: Mars water ice records climate history and is a candidate resource for crews.
applications: Drilling and core handling in permafrost

nasa_documented.summary: NASA's Mars science objectives include an Ice, Weather and Climate goal on how near-surface water ice forms and changes; Perseverance's human-preparation objective covers producing propellant and oxygen from the Martian atmosphere (a different resource); NASA lists ISRU as an analog.

cannot_reproduce: Mars surface pressure (about 6 mbar) and CO2 atmosphere cause rapid ice sublimation
Ice depth, age and purity differ
Mars gravity about 0.38 g

experiments.name: Dust, terrain & thermal equipment evaluation
experiments.what_is_tested: Power and thermal hardware and dust-tolerant components under large temperature swings and dry, barren ground.
experiments.why: Mars surface systems face dust and strong day-night temperature swings; dry high-swing analogs let teams rehearse this.

nasa_documented.summary: Perseverance's human-preparation objective includes measuring atmospheric dust and collecting surface weather data; the sources checked do not describe an Earth-analog dust/thermal campaign.

cannot_reproduce: Martian dust is fine, electrostatic and wind-lofted in a 6 mbar atmosphere
Much higher UV and radiation at the surface
Different atmospheric heat transfer

experiments.name: Habitat, crew operations & simulated EVA missions
experiments.what_is_tested: Crew routines, simulated spacewalks, maintenance and isolation in a harsh, remote setting.
experiments.why: Long-duration crews need operations, health and performance rehearsed in isolated analogs.

nasa_documented.summary: NASA's CHAPEA missions simulate year-long stays on Mars with a crew of four in an isolated habitat, including simulated spacewalks; NASA's analog missions page also lists Antarctic stations and HERA.

cannot_reproduce: Real communication delay and true isolation from Earth
Mars gravity, pressure and radiation
Actual suit and habitat pressure loads
